Use case: illustration-story. Asset: reusable Mochi expression/acting sheet for an original cat IP, not a finished comic.
Reference image 1 is the accepted blue-studio keyframe: strictly preserve Mochi's original fluffy orange-gold kitten, cream muzzle/chest, pink nose and round warm dark eyes; Lucky's warm charcoal BLACK shorter-furred kitten, large pointed ears, small dark nose and yellow-green round eyes. Reference image 2 is the original painting and defines LARGE flat broken matte gouache brush masses and simplified natural kitten proportions. These are our original cats, not upright human mascots. No fine individual-hair rendering, polished shading, airbrush, vector outlines, clothing, human hands, human grins, permanent accessories, or copied franchise characters. Keep connected cat anatomy, consistent small cat mouths and recognizable face/ear/head-body proportions.
Only Mochi appears; fluffy orange-gold coat, cream mouth/chest, tiny pink nose; original orange sister only, no black cat.
Exactly SIX complete drawings, THREE columns by TWO rows in one LANDSCAPE sheet. Each cell contains ONE WHOLE kitten, entire ears, whiskers, shoulders, forelegs, hindquarters, paws and tail comfortably inside its own cell with a generous transparent gutter. GENUINE alpha transparency, no floor, no cast shadow field, no background rectangle. Stable seated natural kitten pose, fixed three-quarter angle, equal scale and common foot baseline across all six cells; acting changes are SMALL and legible in eyes, ears, tiny mouth and head angle, not a new face/body design. Natural cat posture, never crossed arms or human standing body. Do NOT cut the neck or paws, do not isolate floating body parts.
Read left to right then second row: 1 neutral attentive listening; 2 dry sideways skeptical look with a slight eyelid drop; 3 soft slow blink showing trust, mouth closed; 4 genuinely surprised with slightly raised ears and wider original-size eyes, not a giant mouth; 5 secretly delighted, eyes gently curved and a tiny almost invisible pleased mouth, no human smile; 6 sleepy and patiently unimpressed, half-lidded but not angry or contemptuous.
No text, labels, numbers, logo, bubble, frame, watermark or UI. Broad coarse gouache color planes; NOT fine fur. Do not fill every spare pixel with a cat: keep clear gutters so each WHOLE character can later be reused without clipping whiskers or tails. These are distinct acting references, not a claim of smooth sequential animation.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset: ONE original 4:5 vertical scene keyframe for the everyday Mochi & Lucky IP, not a presentation or finished comic.
Reference image 1 is the accepted blue-studio keyframe: strictly preserve Mochi's original fluffy orange-gold kitten, cream muzzle/chest, pink nose and round warm dark eyes; Lucky's warm charcoal BLACK shorter-furred kitten, large pointed ears, small dark nose and yellow-green round eyes. Reference image 2 is the original painting and defines LARGE flat broken matte gouache brush masses and simplified natural kitten proportions. These are our original cats, not upright human mascots. No fine individual-hair rendering, polished shading, airbrush, vector outlines, clothing, human hands, human grins, permanent accessories, or copied franchise characters. Keep connected cat anatomy, consistent small cat mouths and recognizable face/ear/head-body proportions.
Setting: a cozy closed rain-speckled window, muted blue-gray rainy garden outside, warm cream interior and a painted blue floor, a low windowsill safe for kittens.
Acting and staging: Lucky sits RIGHT with both front paws planted, nose close to the closed glass and hopeful eyes fixed on the rain as if waiting for it to stop. Mochi sits LEFT a little farther back, quietly looking from Lucky to a small neat puddle-free row of raindrops running down the glass; her expression gently matter-of-fact. Both entire cats are visible and dry indoors. No raincoat, umbrella, dangerous open window, written weather report or magical sunbeam.
The environment and both cats must be painted as ONE coherent illustration in the same chunky gouache language, with tactile broad brush planes and restrained modeling. Warm orange against painterly blue/cream, with only muted location accents. Cat-eye-level staging, clear silhouettes and a specific small visual relationship, generous ear/paw margins, cats prominent rather than tiny background decorations. Keep natural cat poses, all joints connected; props may naturally occlude bodies but never leave a floating paw or severed neck. Emotion is restrained, affectionate, dryly funny, not mean or slapstick. No computer, laptop, product interface, brand logo, sales message, text, speech bubble, title, labels, border or watermark. No giant empty heading region or beige card layout. Do not copy the original overhead diagonal composition or repeat the studio-table setup. New locations are candidate settings, not a redesign or permanently approved world.
